kiln_p10_001.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_001.text: The clinic's waiting room smelled of boiled linen and the bitter herb somebody had spilled near the stove. Yue sat with her right arm supported against her coat. She wanted to look composed until the examiner asked her to remove it. The ordinary motion hurt enough to stop her halfway. Han helped with the sleeve after asking which movement she could tolerate. Yue hated needing help with cloth more than she expected. The shoulder did not care how much thought she had given to useful limits that winter. It answered the actual reach she tried to make.

kiln_p10_002.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_002.text: The examiner asked her to describe the load and movement before touching the joint. Yue admitted that she had reached higher after the call to set the frame down. Han described the crosswind and the grounded corner. Their accounts agreed on the important sequence without making either person remember every breath. The examiner checked ordinary movement, touch and the signs that would require further urgent assessment. The first finding supported a shoulder strain rather than a displaced joint. It remained an initial finding, with follow-up required. Yue listened as though the word ordinary should somehow make pain less real.

kiln_p10_003.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_003.text: She could move her fingers and felt normal touch at the examined points. Lifting the arm outward brought pain at the outer shoulder. The examiner did not make her prove it repeatedly. She prescribed ordinary protection from the painful load, careful permitted movement and return for any worsening or altered sensation. Cultivation through the affected arm paths paused until the route examiner and physical review agreed on a safe plan. Yue asked whether the stored reserve would damage her while unused. The answer required a qualified circulation review, not guessing from the amount she hoped still lived below her navel.

kiln_p10_004.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_004.text: Luo came after securing the work crew and spoke with the clinic's qualified route examiner. They reviewed Yue's previously learned external trace exit at a healthy contact, with no loaded arm-route task. She followed only that quiet closure and grounding procedure under observation. The retained quantity could fall during rest and sampling without becoming a failure she had to fight. She understood and still felt an urge to preserve every unit, as though losing a number meant losing the months that had produced it. They recorded the actual safe release rather than asking the strained shoulder for another demonstration.

kiln_p10_005.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_005.text: Peng arranged the immediate recovery under the signed employment term. Yue's remaining shift became no shift at all once the examination showed the actual limitation. The owner had included authorised short recovery support rather than paying only people able to hide pain. Longer modified duties would be reviewed against what Yue could do. Peng brought the relevant page and kept it brief. Yue did not need to argue for the entire future while undressing with one good arm. She needed a meal, a place to sleep and the next ordinary appointment she could actually attend.

kiln_p10_006.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_006.text: Han walked her upstairs carrying the pack she suddenly resented. Its familiar strap had become an obstacle. He set it beside the bed and asked whether she wanted anything moved within easy reach. Yue said no too quickly. He waited. She asked for the wash bowl to be lowered and the lamp brought nearer. The small requests embarrassed her more than the medical findings. Han made them ordinary by doing them without a speech. Before leaving, he told her that the frame was tagged out of use. Its future would not require her to get dressed and defend it tonight.

kiln_p10_007.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_007.text: Her roommates returned from work smelling of damp leather and bread. They saw the supported arm and stopped joking before Yue could ask them not to. That hurt too. She described the injury plainly, then said the Wandering Toe had escaped judgment while the shoulder took the blame. One roommate laughed with visible relief. The other helped rearrange the table so Yue could eat without an awkward reach. The room did not become cheerful immediately. It became usable, which was a kinder thing to ask of the first evening.

kiln_p10_008.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_008.text: The first night was poor. Yue woke whenever she shifted toward the injured side, then lay still listening to a loose shutter tap outside. She tried to find a painless position and became angry at the bedding. Her ordinary breath practice offered no secret repair. She breathed normally because holding air would add another problem, then let herself stop trying to make the night educational. Near dawn she slept for an hour. The next morning's report contained that hour rather than an invented recovery. The shoulder felt stiff and the day already looked longer than she wanted.

kiln_p10_009.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_009.text: Zhu arrived with breakfast and no bright advice. She asked where to set the bowl. Yue said the nearest corner, then corrected herself because the left hand would have to cross the table. They moved the bowl again. Zhu had learned the value of asking about exact reach from years with her own limits. Yue apologised for the old offer to carry the failed tray as though injury made a person only a burden. Zhu accepted the apology, then said breakfast was cooling. Care could remain specific enough that neither of them had to become a lesson before eating.

kiln_p10_010.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_010.text: Yue asked how long Zhu had felt furious after the loading-door injury. The trimmer said anger had not respected a clean calendar. Some days she felt practical, some sad and some ashamed of being sad over things others considered small. Learning the left-hand skill helped because it gave her a task, not because it made the old right hand unimportant. Yue listened with a new discomfort. Earlier she had admired that story from outside. Now she recognised the wish to turn recovery into a tidy transformation so that the pain would at least produce an impressive person.

kiln_p10_011.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_011.text: Zhu told her not to borrow the entire older injury as a prediction. Their findings and histories differed. Yue could use the friendship without inheriting the same outcome. The warning felt unexpectedly tender. It left her allowed to hope for recovery without implying Zhu had failed to hope hard enough. They sat quietly while the bread softened in the warm soup. Yue wanted to say something wise and found nothing. She thanked Zhu for breakfast. The small true sentence seemed better than forcing the morning to explain every possible future.

kiln_p10_012.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_012.text: Jian came at noon with a carefully copied update. The final funded cups were still drying, the crew had rearranged Yue's documentation duties and the warning point worked at the cold check. He had written the facts as though good ink might repair her. She thanked him and asked about his own next lesson. He said it had moved around the foreman's clinic visit and would happen later under the current rule. Yue felt guilty. The boy shook his head before she could apologise for being injured. "This is what the rule is for," he said, surprising them both.

kiln_p10_013.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_013.text: He left her the copy and stayed long enough to complain about the heroic cook's knife handling. Yue laughed until the shoulder tugged, then stopped with a sharp face. Jian went quiet. She said laughing could wait for a softer joke, not disappear forever. He offered the story of Han losing bread to a dog with better timing. It worked. They found a way to sit beside pain without pretending it had made every subject solemn. Yue watched him leave and thought the boy could be astonishingly gentle when nobody demanded gratitude or trust before letting him help.

kiln_p10_014.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_014.text: At the first follow-up, the examiner found the ordinary strain had not developed new alarming signs, but the painful outward movement remained limited. Yue had been keeping the permitted quiet movement and avoiding load. The plan continued with a scheduled reassessment rather than a return based on one better hour. She asked whether trying a copper task might tell them more. The route examiner said the ordinary injured structure was already providing enough information. Adding spiritual input to satisfy impatience would blur rather than clarify it. Yue accepted the answer with less grace than she had imagined she would possess.

kiln_p10_015.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_015.text: On the walk home, she envied a woman carrying two ordinary buckets easily. The woman stopped to rest halfway up the lane, and the envy changed shape. Yue had seen only the easy part from a distance. Her own story looked like a capable fourth-stage practitioner resting between useful tasks until somebody saw the difficult sleeve. She sat on the bakery bench and watched steam from the afternoon bread rise into cold air. The world had not divided cleanly into people whose bodies worked and people who had failed. It had remained particular needs.

kiln_p10_016.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_016.text: Peng offered modified archive work after the clinician approved a short seated trial with frequent changes of position. The task used Yue's ordinary left hand and did not involve lifting retained jars or reaching to the upper shelf. The agreed short-day rate was stated before she began. Recovery meals and bed remained under the authorised term. Yue wanted a full shift and knew she could not yet sit comfortably through it. She accepted the smaller task, then felt angry at the smaller coins. Honest arrangements could still leave a person disappointed by the body's actual limit.

kiln_p10_017.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_017.text: The first left-handed copy looked worse than her earliest ordinary talisman exercise. Yue made three numerals uncertain and one almost elegant in the wrong direction. Peng gave her a large practice board before letting the copy enter the working index. The keeper refused to make reassurance into acceptance of unreadable records. She also refused to take the pen away as though difficulty proved Yue could not learn. They practised the actual small movements and shortened the first task. Yue went home tired, with a modest paid result that someone else could read without guessing.

kiln_p10_018.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_018.text: Zhu inspected the private practice page that evening. She praised one clear line and laughed at a numeral resembling a drowning goose. Yue laughed too, more gently this time. The trimmer showed her how to brace the ordinary page so the left hand did not fight its slipping edge. A simple board stop helped more than another speech about resilience. Yue disliked how much she loved such tiny improvements. Her grand next-stage ambition had narrowed for the day to writing a number that did not embarrass the reader. The number mattered because the reader had work to do.

kiln_p10_019.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_019.text: Tan brought the final funded load's current cost summary to the archive while Yue sat at the lower table. He asked whether he should come back later. She said she could review a short packet but not climb for its references. He fetched the matching folder after Peng authorised the ordinary access. The task became cooperative without turning Tan into a healer or Yue into a helpless guest. She found one transport line duplicated from the earlier delivery and asked him to correct it. He did. The shoulder had changed her movement, not removed every useful thing she knew.

kiln_p10_020.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_020.text: Afterward he said her injury made him feel less foolish about being constrained. She disliked the sentence before understanding its intention. He meant that limits were not only punishments for bad conduct. A competent person could need help without becoming worthless. Yue answered that her shoulder was not a comparison designed to comfort him, then softened the edge. She could see the connection, but each case had its own cause. Tan apologised for borrowing her pain too quickly. They sat with the awkwardness until it became small enough to continue the actual work.

kiln_p10_021.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_021.text: That night Yue drafted a letter home and stopped at the injury sentence. She could describe it as a slight delay or make it sound catastrophic. Neither helped her mother plan around the truth. She wrote the initial finding, current limits, paid recovery terms and next reassessment. The left-hand script made the letter look more alarming than the words. She added that the poor handwriting came from learning another ordinary task, not a new mysterious illness. Then she asked Peng to address the cover clearly. Accepting that small help let the rest of the letter remain her own.

kiln_p10_022.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_022.text: Her mother could not reply for days. Yue imagined several possible answers and found none soothing enough to settle the waiting. She put the letter copy away and borrowed another chapter of the absurd cook. The hero had now burned a pot while refusing advice. Yue admired the author's unintentional realism. She read the funniest passage aloud to her roommates, who insisted the bowl cleaner should inherit the mountain. For half an hour the painful shoulder was present without occupying every sentence. The evening did not cure her. It gave her an ordinary place to be while uncured.

kiln_p10_023.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_023.text: The owner visited the following afternoon with the work-incident account. She had set aside a finite ordinary care allowance for the clinic follow-ups required by this documented injury, with further expenses reviewed openly if the case changed. The allowance was support, not a loan against Yue's future wages. Yue had already paid the first small fee from her personal purse; Peng arranged its recorded reimbursement. She felt relief and an immediate fear that relief made her indebted in some larger invisible way. The owner asked only for the actual receipts and honest recovery information.

kiln_p10_024.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_024.text: The incident review found the loose crosspiece on the earlier rejected frame and the sound frame's later wind movement were separate events. No one used the first fault to pretend the second frame should never have been lifted. The sheltered route had been inspected, but the door opening admitted a gust during the final carry. Han's set-down call came in time; Yue's reflexive high reach changed her shoulder position after it. The review recommended an ordinary wind screen and a lower controlled handling arrangement. It recorded her movement without making the whole accident a story of personal recklessness.

kiln_p10_025.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_025.text: Luo brought her that account and asked whether it matched her memory. She corrected one detail about where her right hand had been. He accepted the change after Han confirmed it. The altered position made the strain's mechanism clearer. Yue had wanted the report to absolve her of every mistake and dreaded one that blamed her for all of it. The actual account offered neither comfort. It offered a process they could change and an ordinary movement she could learn not to repeat. She signed the reviewed sequence and cried after the foreman left.

kiln_p10_026.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_026.text: The crying surprised her because the injury was not severe in the way she had feared. She still had treatment, a bed, friends and useful work. None of those facts prevented grief over a body that hurt when she laughed. Zhu found her with wet cheeks and said no one required a worst injury before permitting sadness. Yue laughed weakly at needing that stated. The trimmer sat beside her until the feeling passed into exhaustion. They did not make a recovery plan during the tears. There would be enough ordinary plans after she ate.

kiln_p10_027.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_027.text: At the next appointment, the ordinary range had improved slightly without load. The examiner added a carefully limited movement and showed what pain should stop it. Yue tried once under observation. She wanted to complete another because the first looked unimpressive. The examiner stopped the repetition before it became a private test of will. The purpose was to find a tolerable movement, not exhaust it. Yue wrote the instruction in large left-handed letters. The goose-shaped numeral survived on the practice sheet, a reminder that learning could be ridiculous while the actual work stayed serious.

kiln_p10_028.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_028.text: She spent the next days between short archive periods and quiet ordinary movement. The hours passed slowly until the archive gave her a difficult index question, then too quickly until the shoulder demanded a change of position. Peng arranged a low shelf within reach and assigned lifting to another paid worker. The modified task was not a favor owed personally to the keeper. It belonged to the employer's reviewed arrangement. That distinction made Yue brave enough to request the next necessary adjustment instead of waiting until discomfort turned into an impressive display of endurance.

kiln_p10_029.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_029.text: Jian asked whether she missed actual practice. She said yes, fiercely. He had expected a calm lesson about accepting limits and looked pleased by the honest answer. They read the primary-route chart together, with no admission through it. Yue could still explain why the third and fourth proposed pairs were distinct. The shoulder rest did not turn the anatomy into nonsense or open a leg route to compensate. Jian asked whether she feared falling behind. She said the question behind falling was behind whom. He looked away because he knew exactly whom he compared himself with.

kiln_p10_030.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_030.text: His father had written that a neighbor's son already held a clerk post. Jian described the comparison angrily, then admitted the other boy had studied account work for years. The fact did not comfort him. Yue said she could feel envy and still refuse to borrow another person's history as evidence against her own. He accused her of sounding like Su Yan. She answered that Su Yan would probably ask them both to eat before turning family pressure into a cultivation method. Jian laughed, and they went to the shared meal at its actual hour.

kiln_p10_031.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_031.text: Tan came to the modified work table with an estimate requiring two ordinary shipment dates. Yue noticed that one date assumed the final cups passed before they had even fired. He corrected it under the current rule, then apologised for repeating a familiar kind of shortcut. She said the checked process had caught it before a commitment. That mattered too. His probation did not require every draft to arrive perfect. It required him to submit decisions through review rather than hide uncertainty until it became someone else's unavoidable duty. He looked less crushed after hearing that distinction.

kiln_p10_032.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_032.text: The final twelve-piece load entered the kiln while Yue remained away from live duties. She received the ordinary work summary after her short archive task, not a demand to attend. Luo and the qualified replacement observer handled the actual shift. The warning point worked under the current handover. Yue imagined missing a decisive moment and then reminded herself that useful processes should survive one person's absence. The thought felt noble until she admitted it also made her feel replaceable. She told Zhu, who said being needed and being impossible to replace were not always the same blessing.

kiln_p10_033.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_033.text: Zhu had once tried to keep the entire trimming station dependent on her after the injury. It made her feel valuable and left her exhausted. Teaching Han part of the work had felt like surrender before it became relief. Yue listened while the trimmer described a week of poor sleep and unkind remarks she later regretted. The story lacked the polished courage of her earlier account. Yue loved it more. A friend could offer the rough version of a change, where kindness had to be repaired and practical help learned through irritation.

kiln_p10_034.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_034.text: After proper cooling, the final funded shelf produced ten ordinary candidates from twelve pieces. Two had forming faults outside the retained condition. The guarded release review accepted eight candidates under the specified method, yielding twenty-seven qualified cups across the three funded loads. Twenty-four would fulfill the new commission; three remained separately identified under the owner's agreed reserve provision rather than silently become free extras owed to the purchaser. The failed pieces kept their histories. The job had used its finite development allowance and reached its promised result without converting every clay object into a success.

kiln_p10_035.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_035.text: Peng brought the completed count to Yue's lower table. Yue checked the identities against the first nineteen already delivered and the final transfer plan. She found no missing qualification or doubled identity. The work was satisfying because it needed her knowledge rather than her shoulder. Tan arranged the last five required deliveries with the instructor. The contract closed only after the user's inspection and acknowledged histories. Yue felt happy for the hall and sad to have missed the firing. Both feelings could sit beside a correct account without requiring one to disprove the other.

kiln_p10_036.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_036.text: The instructor visited to thank the crew. She described the beginner room adjusting to smaller groups, using the sound delivered vessels and keeping the unqualified rival batch guarded. The association was seeking a refund from its supplier through the actual purchase terms. The kiln's smaller fair commission had not solved every earlier promise to parents. It had provided twenty-four defined tools that the room could responsibly use. Yue asked about the learner who had requested a stop. The instructor said the learner had returned and completed a later permitted demonstration. Yue smiled without claiming the event as her own achievement.

kiln_p10_037.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_037.text: Han put a plain banner over the supper table reading Twenty-Four Cups, Fewer Lies. Peng made him take it down because the phrase accused more than the completed contract established. He complained that accuracy ruined celebrations. Zhu proposed Twenty-Four Cups, Adequate Soup. The owner approved that title and supplied actual beans. Yue attended with her supported arm and laughed at the smaller banner. The celebration did not require every failed piece to vanish. They ate beside the knowledge that eight final candidates had become the five deliveries they needed, with a few sound reserves and many honest rejects.

kiln_p10_038.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_038.text: Jian made the speech by pretending to be the heroic cook's bowl cleaner. He demanded payment for all forgotten meals and threatened to found a higher realm of dishwashing. Han surrendered his spoon as tribute. Tan negotiated a plain receipt. Yue laughed carefully and felt the shoulder pull less sharply than the week before. That small physical change pleased her more than she wanted to admit. It was not clinical clearance and did not become permission for a load. It was an ordinary moment she could enjoy without asking it to carry the future.

kiln_p10_039.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_039.text: After the supper, Luo reminded her not to help stack the heavy pots. Yue had already reached with her good hand. The correction irritated her, then saved her from lifting a weight that would have tugged the resting shoulder through compensation. She returned to folding cloths on the low table. Jian joined her and said smaller jobs were still jobs, almost apologetically. She accepted the company and the truth without pretending the truth made the smaller job her favorite. They folded enough clean cloths for the next ordinary day and left the lifting to the actual assigned crew.

kiln_p10_040.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_040.text: Su Yan's arrival was delayed by a road closure until the fourteenth week's beginning. The news disappointed Yue, who had imagined the teacher naming a clear plan before then. The clinic checks continued and the existing practice pause stayed in place. Peng did not let the delayed circuit silently become lost wages or an extra training fee. The preparation review could wait under its stated terms. Yue read the message, then put it away and practised the ordinary left-handed script. Hope had a new date. The day still had a task she could finish without moving the injured joint.

kiln_p10_041.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_041.text: Her mother's letter arrived before Su Yan. It began with the shoulder rather than the wages and ended with instructions to let someone else carry the wash water. Yue smiled at the specificity. Her mother had strained an ordinary wrist once and remembered how quickly pride could turn an easy errand into a renewed pain. She did not tell Yue the accident was secretly a gift. She said she was glad the frame had not trapped her, and glad the clinic had seen her promptly. Gratitude and discomfort could be true together without making injury desirable.

kiln_p10_042.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_042.text: Yue read the letter twice, then let herself miss home. The west kiln's familiar sounds came back: a door latch, the scrape of an ordinary wooden bowl, her mother's short breath when lifting a badly placed sack. She had once wanted to leave those sounds behind. Now she wanted to carry enough of them that a new place could not convince her ordinary care was beneath cultivation. She wrote a reply in her improving left hand and included a plain drawing of the lower archive table. Her mother would understand its useful height better than any heroic description.

kiln_p10_043.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_043.text: Zhu saw the drawing and asked whether Yue had made the table look more elegant than it was. Yue admitted the leg had been straightened on paper. Zhu made her add the ordinary wedge that kept it level. They laughed, and the picture became a small accurate object Yue was proud to send. The shoulder still disliked certain movements. The left-hand script no longer looked like a goose fleeing danger. Neither improvement justified more physical load. They were useful things she could enjoy while another useful thing remained unavailable.

kiln_p10_044.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_044.text: At the clinic, the next ordinary examination showed less pain within the prescribed movement and no new altered sensation. The plan advanced carefully to a small unloaded range task, with the painful direction still protected. Yue wanted a date for full return. The examiner offered a review point, not a guarantee. The phrase disappointed her less than before, because she had seen what guaranteed dates did to cups and fuel. Bodies were not vessels in every respect, but they too could be made harder to understand when a desired calendar replaced their actual response.

kiln_p10_045.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_045.text: Su Yan arrived on a bright cold morning carrying her own ordinary travel account and a tired expression. She had spent the delay treating her circuit as a set of changed appointments rather than racing the closed road. Yue met her at the lower table. The teacher asked for the physical findings, current safe release record and actual sleep before asking how the student felt about lost practice. Yue said she felt cheated by her own shoulder. Su Yan laughed softly. The shoulder had no commission to meet, even if its owner had written one privately.

kiln_p10_046.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_046.text: They reviewed the incident without adding a spiritual cause. Yue had reached poorly under an ordinary changing load. Current arm-route tasks paused because their surrounding tissue was recovering. The earned fourth-stage record remained an account of earlier demonstrated capacity. Present usable work could be smaller. Su Yan did not lower the record to punish her or clear current practice because the record looked impressive. She marked the pause and the conditions for reconsidering it. Yue felt relieved by the exactness. Her past work survived, and her present pain no longer had to compete with it.

kiln_p10_047.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_047.text: The teacher inspected the healthy external trace exit under the clinic route examiner's observation. Yue performed only the quiet permitted grounding already reviewed, not a loaded arm test. Her reserve after poor sleep and rest had fallen from its settled-work plateau. Compatibility remained within the current observed history, with no claim that injured weeks had met the new ninety-percent goal. They recorded the lower usable result without increasing admission. The number looked disappointingly ordinary. Su Yan said a record that could honestly shrink was more trustworthy than one that grew whenever its owner was afraid.

kiln_p10_048.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_048.text: They closed the first preparation block as reviewed work completed within its actual scope, with interrupted practice and injury clearly recorded. The next block became ordinary rehabilitation, chart study, quiet permitted maintenance and independent physical follow-up. No new leg admission would begin while the shoulder's posture and arm release remained unsettled. The owner renewed only the finite support needed for that reviewed block. Yue did not owe a stage in exchange for the cost. She owed honest participation in the arrangement she accepted, and useful paid work within the modified tasks her body could actually perform.

kiln_p10_049.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_049.text: Su Yan asked whether she wanted to leave the training plan. Yue said no quickly, then considered before saying it again. Staying meant weeks of smaller work and uncertain pace. Leaving would not heal the shoulder sooner. The teacher approved the second answer because it had arrived after a real choice. Yue had learned enough to know that persistence could become another way of hiding fear if she refused ever to reconsider. This time she remained because the actual plan, people and work still made sense. The shoulder did not need to be consulted as an enemy.

kiln_p10_050.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_050.text: They spent an hour on anatomy and the new pairs with an uncharged model. Yue named the anterior foot, knee and hip path, then the distinct posterior heel and calf return. The chart remained useful during rest without turning an unopened leg route into a substitute for the injured arm. Su Yan asked her to explain why a new channel could not compensate for careless shoulder lifting. Yue answered with the frame's weight and her changed reach, not a proverb. The teacher nodded. She had found a student less interested in an impressive sentence than in a correct cause.

kiln_p10_051.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_051.text: That afternoon, Su Yan watched Luo's current ordinary teaching review. The foreman had made the wind screen and lower handling arrangement part of the frame task, with the maintenance worker checking its real stability. He would not ask apprentices to perform that work simply because the materials were ordinary. Yue listened from the permitted low station. The changes could reduce a recurrence. They did not make her shoulder heal retroactively. She liked that the hall could learn without treating her body as a necessary price everyone should celebrate.

kiln_p10_052.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_052.text: At supper, Han asked the examiner whether the new rehabilitation block counted as cultivation. Su Yan said it counted as keeping a cultivator able to live through another lesson, which made Yue remember Yun's old words about Skin. The memory warmed her more than the soup. She had not graduated beyond the principle; she had found a new reason to need it. Han wanted the phrase on the wall. Peng said the wall already held enough instructions and suggested they simply offer the injured person a chair at the right height.

kiln_p10_053.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_053.text: Jian watched the teacher sit beside Yue and later asked whether important people became more patient at higher stages. Su Yan said some became more difficult to persuade because power had protected their worst habits. A larger reserve was not a moral assessment. The boy looked both delighted and worried. Yue liked the answer because it refused to make cultivation a ladder into automatic wisdom. Su Yan could teach a method and still need road conditions, ordinary soup and colleagues who corrected her. The fifth stage Yue wanted would add routes, not certify every future choice as good.

kiln_p10_054.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_054.text: Before leaving, the examiner reviewed the coming weeks with the clinic and foreman. Physical clearance would precede low-load arm reassessment; normal following-day findings would determine whether progression continued. New-route instruction waited beyond that recovery and a renewed preparation review. Su Yan's next circuit date remained a date, not an instant rescue summons. She gave Yue one practical task: write what her shoulder could actually do each day without comparing it to the imagined uninjured version. Yue disliked the assignment enough to suspect it would be useful.

kiln_p10_055.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_055.text: The first page was short. I can eat with my left hand. I can write clearly if I rest. I cannot reach the upper shelf. Yue nearly added I should be able to, then crossed the phrase out while leaving it readable in the private margin. The present shoulder had not signed her expectation. She could acknowledge grief without turning it into a movement. Zhu read the page at Yue's invitation and said it needed one more line: I can ask for the bowl to be placed nearer. Yue added it, laughing quietly.

kiln_p10_056.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_056.text: During the next modified archive shift, a jar reference lay beyond her approved reach. She called the assigned lifting worker rather than stretch because everyone looked busy. He brought it to the low bench without irritation. The moment felt embarrassingly easy after so much internal argument. Yue checked the body label, returned the original through the same worker and completed the useful comparison. No dramatic self-conquest appeared on the daily page. A simple requested movement had kept the record usable and the shoulder out of an unnecessary test.

kiln_p10_057.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_057.text: Peng then asked her to review a received copy of the association's rival batch certificate against the shared method note. The instructor had obtained it while seeking the supplier's refund. Yue could do this seated and within the offered record scope. The certificate named a workshop assessor whose signature resembled Luo's familiar heavy slash. The name was different. The date referred to a day when Luo's own record placed him in this hall. She marked the resemblance as a question, not a forgery finding, and asked Peng to obtain a clearer authorised copy.

kiln_p10_058.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_058.text: The keeper agreed and kept the current commission's qualified histories separate from the rival dispute. A similar signature could arise innocently, and a copy could distort a stroke. The requested comparison concerned which actual assessor had witnessed the supplied method. Yue felt a new mystery rise into the quiet work, then resisted leaning physically toward it as though better posture could improve the evidence. She called for a second lamp placed within reach. The shoulder's small refusal had begun teaching her to notice the difference between urgency and the actual movement it demanded.

kiln_p10_059.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_059.text: Zhu teased her about finding excitement in a chair-bound packet. Yue said the chair had not made winter less complicated. The trimmer looked at the unclear signature and frowned, remembering the old apprentice record whose missing transfer had followed her for years. Paper could hold work, hide it or pretend another person's work had happened. Neither woman made the unclear mark answer more than it could. They left the copy with Peng and went to the lower supper table. The next investigation could wait while the person conducting it ate.

kiln_p10_060.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_060.text: Yue's daily shoulder page gained another modest line near the week's end: the permitted unloaded movement hurts less. It did not say healed. The clinic confirmed the improvement and kept the next review. Yue felt hopeful without borrowing tomorrow's clearance. She had discovered a pace that belonged neither to surrender nor to the pursuit of a perfect streak. Some days remained angry and dull. Some contained a readable left-handed sentence, a good joke or a new question worth asking. The shoulder kept its ordinary answer, and she had begun listening without requiring it to flatter her.

kiln_p10_061.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_061.text: Zhu's neighbor sent word that the low stool still suited her recovering knee. She invited them for tea in the small room where she had first tested its height. Yue hesitated, fearing a visit would require cheerful usefulness she lacked. Zhu told her they were guests, not a repair service. The neighbor placed the cups within ordinary reach and asked about the heroic cook. Yue recounted his latest disaster, laughing gently enough for the shoulder. An hour passed in a room where nobody needed her to be stronger than she was.

kiln_p10_062.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_062.text: Walking home, she thanked Zhu for the visit and then apologised for being dull company lately. Zhu stopped so abruptly that Yue nearly passed her. "You are allowed to have a boring month," she said. "I did not befriend a performance." The words made Yue look down at the slushy lane. She had wanted to earn every kindness by returning something useful at once. Zhu linked her own sound arm lightly with Yue's left and they continued, choosing the clear ground together. The town contained company as well as tasks.

kiln_p10_063.speaker: narrator
kiln_p10_063.text: On the last evening of the fourteenth week, she sat with Zhu beside the bakery's warm brick. They watched workers cross the lane with bundles, each carrying a weight neither could know at a distance. Yue said she missed feeling capable without thinking. Zhu said she had never been capable without thinking; she had only forgotten some thinking already done. Yue laughed at the distinction. It was comforting without being false. They shared bread and let the conversation stop before it became advice. The next month would contain smaller work, and enough life to make that work worth doing.
